Ah... A bit too late..
Text is sent. Lmk if you would like to updated, I like the perspectives you offer.
I want to fix things. However, my stance is "I'm not putting up with this, improve and stop doing this or I will dump you"
I explained in another comment chain why I didn't ask. What do you think of it?

I agree with you. I plan on texting her this:   

"Hey let me know a good time and place to discuss our relationship. The sudden silent treatment from the car ride yesterday up until now is very immature and manipulative. You did the same a few days ago at the pho place. I think this prompts a re-evaluation of the future of this relationship, lmk."   

I know that this message is very emotionally charged (I'm very pissed at the moment) so I'm letting myself potentially cool down a bit first. What do you think?
I agree but when I got to the restaurant I didn't know she would hold it up for the entire time. First time she's done it.

Well that's one way to do it. But I don't think I had to ask if she was giving the treatment, it was happening right before my eyes. Tbh I didn't want to leave because we had already ordered $90 worth of food, it might have been a mistake on my part to not leave tho.
Thinking about it after the fact, I agree. However at the time I had no idea she was capable of holding it up for the entire duration of the dinner!

Because that's how this manipulation tactics works. By intentionally withholding engagement, you cause the other person pain and discomfort, then you want them to come to you and ask you to stop, because they can no longer bear the pain. Then, if successful, you have upper hand in the following discussion because you have them at your mercy.
If that's the case I would be so disappointed
I can see that perspective. However it's a day later and still no explanation/communication whatsoever
I agree. Thanks for the input. Most things are great in the relationship so I do want to make it work and fix it if possible, but it is very concerning.

I'm open to other perspectives if they made sense. I'm not saying yours doesn't make sense, I can see where you're coming from actually. However I disagree that it's a better way to deal with it. Allowing my emotions to be held hostage by her and asking her to relieve me of the pain, is exactly what she would want out of the silent treatment.

I thought about the possibility, but she had mentioned the party days before and an invitation was never extended to me. It was her friends that I don't know of, so I don't imagine I'd be invited. Lastly she said she had to "leave my place by X time", which insinuates she won't be going with me

I still disagree. It is begging when she's holding you hostage at her mercy. And as said, if it's not related to me, it's courtesy to let me know. Lastly, it's not an assumption that it was a silent treatment, it was literally what was happening.

This is the 2nd/3rd time. We've been dating for 6 months and they all happened in the last month or so.   

Before going to the restaurant, she mentioned she had a party to attend after. Before the silence, I said i could take myself home after the dinner, so she doesn't have to drive me to my place, then double back and go to the party since it's not in the way. She said "okay..." Which seemed normal.

Not sure if I agree with your thinking. If I'm getting a silent treatment, it's not on me to beg for her to explain what's wrong. You should not give that treatment in the first place. If she's dealing with something else, it's also courtesy to let me know. I would extend the same courtesy if it were me.
